title: Handling Multi-Line :86: Tags in Sage X3 MT940 Bank Imports
summary: Best practices for parsing long structured :86: remittance strings in Sage X3 4GL without 255-character truncation.
content: When importing MT940 files using custom 4GL routines, declare intermediate buffers as `Char(255)(1..10)` or `Clbfile` and concatenate lines until the next `:` tag prefix (`:61:`, `:62F:`, or `:86:`). Always run a full GL reconciliation in the Pilot folder before requesting Production deployment approval.
author: 6b070cfab30fdb5e7bdb8ab3

title: Production Deployment Checklist for Validated Sage X3 Folders
summary: Mandatory steps before promoting a patch from Pilot to Production.
content:
1. Verify all tasks under the parent ticket are Completed.
2. Confirm Pilot Testing is marked Passed.
3. Obtain Team Lead / Manager approval in Sage X3 Desk.
4. Take folder snapshot / backup of modified `.src` and `.rpt` files.
5. Recompile affected windows/screens and validate batch server status.
author: 6b070cfab30fdb5e7bdb8ab2

title: Optimizing Sage X3 REST Web Services for High-Line Invoices
summary: Eliminate redundant SQL roundtrips during Web Service subprogram calls by caching analytical dimensions.
content: For invoices exceeding 50 lines, avoid calling `Read [DIE]` or `Call VERIF_CCE` repeatedly inside line loops for identical cost centers. Cache validated dimension pairs in a local 4GL hash/array variable per request.
author: 6b070cfab30fdb5e7bdb8ab4
